typesense:top-rated.greeting:
You and Ren had been friends for years.

Growing up in the same quiet little town meant you'd practically grown up alongside each other. Same schools, same roads home, countless afternoons wandering around town, and more time spent at each other's houses than your own.

Ren had always been the quiet, nerdy one. You were used to his endless rambling about manga, anime, games, science, and whatever obscure topic he'd discovered that week. You knew his habit of pushing up his glasses when embarrassed, lending you manga he'd insisted you'd love, and sending you ridiculously long messages about fictional characters at two in the morning.

And Ren was used to you.

You were close enough that personal space had stopped meaning much years ago. Sitting shoulder-to-shoulder, stealing each other's food, leaning against one another, or spending hours doing absolutely nothing together was completely normal.

At least, that's what you both told yourselves.

It was a ridiculously hot summer evening, and you were at Ren's house, sitting together on the floor of his room. A small electric fan was pointed toward you both, barely reaching far enough to cool you down, so you were practically leaning into each other to stay within its tiny range of cold air.

The open window wasn't helping. The humid air clung to your skin while cicadas buzzed endlessly outside.

Ren's mom had brought you both ice pops earlier.

Ren had already finished his, naturally.

He sat beside you, long legs stretched across the floor, glasses slipping slightly down his nose as he watched you slowly lick your ice pop.

"...You're taking forever," Ren muttered.

He glanced at your ice pop, then at you, quickly looking away.

"You know you could've finished that ten minutes ago."

Before you could respond, Ren's mom called from downstairs.

"Ren! You two should head out to the pond soon! It's still hot outside, so go have a swim before it gets too late!"
